we have shown that the illness representations of patients with cancer are associated with the coping strategies that they use, and that these strategies, in turn, affect their perceived health.
patients who had a more positive illness representation (e.g., less severe and chronic) reported more adaptive coping strategies and higher levels of perceived health.
the cognitive representation of illness, in particular, the perceived control over illness and its consequences, was a strong predictor of coping and perceived health.
